notes:
1. Dek says the four stories "all landed on the same day". Sources: TechCrunch on Slok is posted "October 25, 2026"; CNBC says Musk posted "on Sunday" (25 Oct); Anthropic's filing and the Itaú notice are 26 Oct. Fix: "all surfaced within two days" (or drop the time claim).
2. Title says "first hard questions". No source says these are the first; TechCrunch says "Recent studies have also found that AI has yet to deliver significant productivity gains" and CNBC says investors were "already questioning" neocloud debt. Fix: drop "first", e.g. "AI's spending is meeting hard questions".
3. Section 2 heading "Meanwhile, a bank buys its AI team" and the text present the purchase as done, and omit the conditions. Source: "The closing of the transaction is subject to the approvals of certain conditions precedent, including prior approval by the Brazilian Antitrust Authority (CADE) and the Central Bank of Brazil". Also "NeoSpace's management and business operations will remain autonomous". Fix: heading "Meanwhile, a bank agrees to buy its AI supplier" (or similar), and add "Closing is subject to approval by the Brazilian Antitrust Authority (CADE) and the Central Bank of Brazil."
4. Section 4 heading "Debt markets are picking sides" states as fact what the source gives as Musk's view ("As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money...", Musk said on X), and "picking sides" is in no source. Fix: "Musk says debt markets are shutting neoclouds out" or similar.
5. Brief 2026-10-26-anthropic-files-s-1-ipo, note: "audited-style numbers on a lab many banks already buy from". No source says the figures are "audited-style" or that many banks buy from Anthropic. Fix: remove that claim, e.g. "The filing gives lenders and investors reported numbers, though the share price and amount raised are still open."
6. Brief 2026-10-26-itau-buys-neospace, note: "the team that already builds its credit, CRM and fraud models points to banks wanting those capabilities in house". Source: NeoSpace has been "developing models trained on Itaú's proprietary data" and the relationship "has already delivered significant and transformative results in areas such as credit, CRM ... and fraud prevention"; Itaú calls it "another step in Itaú's strategy to enhance its proprietary artificial intelligence capabilities". It does not say NeoSpace builds those three models, and one bank's deal does not show what "banks" want. Fix: "Itaú describes the purchase as a step in its strategy to build its own AI capabilities."
7. Brief 2026-10-26-apollo-slok-zero-financial-payoff-outside-tech, note: "it says little about AI spending inside banks and asset managers". The S&P 493 is the S&P 500 minus seven tech names ("Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla"), so it includes large banks and asset managers; the source does not support "says little". Fix: "The claim covers the S&P 500 outside seven large tech stocks, a group that includes banks and asset managers."
